MOVE below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress; 106.31 is moderate. SOFR is secured overnight funding, not unsecured bank funding. NFCI below zero indicates looser-than-average broad financial conditions; -0.478 is a weekly Nov 13 reading, not a live measure.

Fed & Policy Watch
  • SOFR 3.91% effective Nov 19; NFCI -0.478 for week ending Nov 13; MOVE 106.31 and 10-year Treasury 4.92% on Nov 20. These are lagged observations, not live funding measures. Next NFCI release: Nov 25, 8:30 AM ET, week ending Nov 20.
  • Beige Book scheduled Nov 25 at 2:00 PM ET on the dated Board calendar; Chicago Fed gives 3:00 PM ET as its general time (discrepancy flagged below). October FOMC minutes were released Nov 18 at 2:00 PM and are elapsed. Next FOMC meeting Dec 8-9; statement Dec 9 at 2:00 PM, press conference 2:30 PM.
  • Thanksgiving: Board marks Nov 26 as a holiday and says daily/weekly statistical releases scheduled that day move to Nov 27. Selected verified Friday entries include claims, Census Advance Economic Indicators and H.4.1.
  • Energy/market structure: EIA petroleum follows standard Wednesday 10:30 AM ET schedule Nov 25; natural gas storage is listed for noon. TreasuryDirect lists 13-week and 26-week bill bid closings at 11:30 AM and a 2-year note at 1:00 PM today.
  • Upcoming: BEA October Personal Income and Outlays (PCE) Dec 2; Employment Situation Dec 4; FOMC Dec 9; CPI Dec 10; PPI Dec 15. CPI and PPI are distinct releases.
Omissions and Watch
  • Date conflict check: New York Fed November calendar lists Personal Income and the PCE Deflator on Nov 25 at 8:30 AM; BEA direct schedule lists Personal Income and Outlays for October on Dec 2 at 8:30 AM and for November on Dec 23 at 8:30 AM. To preserve the date-specific New York Fed listing, Nov 25 is shown with an explicit conflict warning; do not assume it refers to the same release. Confirm against an official update. The BEA-confirmed Oct release is separately listed Dec 2.
  • Beige Book time conflict: Federal Reserve Board's date-specific calendar states Nov 25 at 2:00 PM ET; Chicago Fed gives a general Beige Book release time of 3:00 PM ET. The Board date-specific time is displayed with caveat.
  • Richmond Fed and Conference Board schedule pages did not load reliably through the available route; Nov 24 dates/times are from the date-specific New York Fed calendar. Philadelphia Fed survey date/time is also cited to the New York Fed calendar.
  • BLS pages were not requested; BLS release dates/times were checked on the New York Fed Economic Indicators Calendar. Periods not shown by that calendar are not inferred. The classifier self-test passed; unmatched rows are provisional Medium with review notes.
  • Selected events from checked primary calendars, not exhaustive; Fed statistical releases are selected, including H.4.1. EIA dates follow its official standard schedules and listed exceptions. No selected calendar row was verified for Thanksgiving Day; no claim is made about exchange hours.
  • Sources checked: New York Fed November/December calendars and SOFR API; Federal Reserve Board November/December calendars, FOMC calendar and H.4.1; BEA; Census; EIA petroleum/natural gas schedules; TreasuryDirect; U.S. Treasury; Chicago Fed; Philadelphia Fed schedule route. Market quotes are single-source Yahoo Finance; yields are official Treasury data.
  • No verified unscheduled policy or geopolitical watch item from this run; this is not a full headline-risk review. Material verified watches: funding/conditions, Treasury supply, holiday-adjusted energy releases, Beige Book timing, and the BEA/New York Fed PCE date conflict.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
Friday SPY fell 3.64%, VIX jumped to 35.89 and MOVE rose to 106.31; the 10-year yield fell 12 bp to 4.92%. ES is higher overnight, but that rebound is not confirmation of a trend change. Monday's activity readings and Treasury supply, Tuesday's confidence/regional surveys, and Wednesday's GDP, durables, NFCI, energy reports and Beige Book arrive ahead of a holiday-thinned week. Prioritize rates, breadth and liquidity confirmation; avoid assuming overnight direction persists. Scenario framing only, not a trade signal.
INVALIDATION
Reassess if ES gives back its overnight recovery as volatility extends, or data, auction demand or the Beige Book materially reprice yields. No unsupported levels or targets supplied. Refresh quotes and verify contract specifications and holiday-session liquidity before execution.
